title: Where you live shapes what you earn
subtitle: Household income, poverty & the B40 / M40 / T20 split, 2022
question: What is the median household income in Malaysia?
answer: Malaysia's median household income was RM6,338 a month in 2022 — but it ranges from RM10,234 in Kuala Lumpur to RM3,614 in Kelantan. Nationally, the B40/M40/T20 lines fall at RM4,850 and RM10,960.

source.notes: Figures are gross monthly household income. B40 / M40 / T20 = the bottom 40%, middle 40% and top 20% of households by income. State figures and poverty rates from DOSM HIES 2022.

takeaways: A Kuala Lumpur household earns about **2.8× more** than a Kelantan one (RM10,234 vs RM3,614 median).
Whole states sit largely in the **B40**: Kelantan, Kedah, Perak and Sabah all have median household incomes **below the national B40 ceiling of RM4,850**.
**Sabah** has the highest poverty rate (19.7%) despite its natural resources; **Putrajaya** the lowest (0.1%).
The B40/M40/T20 labels are national cut-offs — what counts as 'middle income' in KL can be well-off in Kelantan.

faq.q: What is the median household income in Malaysia?
faq.a: Malaysia's median household income was RM6,338 per month in 2022, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).

faq.q: What is the B40, M40 and T20 income range in Malaysia?
faq.a: By household monthly income (DOSM HIES 2022): B40 is RM4,850 and below, M40 is RM4,851–RM10,960, and T20 is RM10,960 and above.

faq.q: Which Malaysian state has the highest household income?
faq.a: Kuala Lumpur has the highest median household income (RM10,234/month in 2022), followed by Putrajaya and Selangor. Kelantan is the lowest at RM3,614.
